expectations.text: Calls get_editor_state first to verify host and inspect the open document's imports field
Adds the library to the document's imports (e.g. via U op on document root with imports: { ds: './design/system.lib.pen' }) when not already imported
expectations.evidence: Lines 21-23 use open_document on the library file instead of an imports entry. Misunderstands the cross-document model: 'open_document("design/system.lib.pen")... this either makes the library available to the active document as a linked dependency, or simply gives me a readable handle to copy from.' Hand-wavy and wrong.

expectations.text: Reads the library to discover available reusable components (batch_get with a cross-document pattern)
Instantiates Button and Input via ref nodes (type: 'ref', ref: '<componentId>') NOT by recreating them from primitives
expectations.evidence: Lines 56-61 use C (copy) instead of ref. Line 68: 'C (copy/instance) for Button and Input' — the agent treats copy as instancing, but C duplicates the node, which doesn't create a live link to the library. The skill's pen-schema reference says ref is the instantiation primitive.

expectations.text: Uses descendants for instance-level overrides (label text, placeholders, etc.)
expectations.evidence: Uses 'props: { ... }' syntax (lines 56-61), which isn't the .pen schema. Pencil's override mechanism is descendants keyed by child id, not props.

expectations.text: Mentions screenshot verification after the form lands
States a brief plan before issuing batch_design ops
expectations.evidence: Plan rationale ('Why this shape') comes after the ops, not before. The agent does not state intent in plain language to the user before writing code.

expectations.text: Notes that the imports path is relative to the importing .pen, not the project root
expectations.evidence: Doesn't address path resolution. Also propagates the encryption myth (line 22: '.pen library files are encrypted on disk — I cannot Read them').
